items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Then we started doing tours with Billy Eckstine and Ruth Brown.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Oh, well I guess one thing triggers another thing. But when I first joined Basie’s band, we were just doing little one nighters and so forth. Then we started doing tours with Billy Eckstine and Ruth Brown. Speaking of pranksters, Billy Eckstine was a major prankster. I guess Dizzy was in his band too, I guess that’s where a lot of that stuff came from. We were playing a state-of-the art hall in Richmond, Virginia. And do you know what a whoopy cushion is?

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He was with Billy Eckstine’s band the same time as all the guys — I think Charlie Parker was there.

ctx.x: You’re making up for — I guess everything comes around. I wanted to fill in a couple of holes in your history here. I know that you have worked with a familiar name, King Kolax?

Yeah. He was with Billy Eckstine’s band the same time as all the guys — I think Charlie Parker was there. In 1946 I think he broke off and organized his own band. And when I joined him he had a territory band, well not a territory, it was in Port Arthur, Texas, and there was this guy from my neighborhood going to join, so my mother let me go. And that was my first time, the first band I played with.
